Inverse dynamics with the recursive Newton-Euler algorithm

Source: R/dynamics.R
robot_inverse_dynamics.Rd

Computes the joint forces and torques \(\tau = M(q)\ddot q + C(q, \dot q)\dot q + g(q) - J^\top f_{ext}\) for a fixed-base rigid-body tree in \(O(n)\) operations. Gravity is a world-frame acceleration vector (default \((0, 0, -9.81)\) m/s^2). External wrenches are given per link as c(force, moment) in world axes with the moment taken about the link frame origin. Joint friction, damping, motor inertia and contact are not modeled.

Usage

robot_inverse_dynamics(
  robot,
  q,
  qd = NULL,
  qdd = NULL,
  gravity = c(0, 0, -9.81),
  f_ext = NULL
)

Arguments

robot

A robot_model with inertial parameters.

q, qd, qdd

Joint positions, velocities and accelerations.

gravity

Gravity vector in world coordinates.

f_ext

Optional named list of external wrenches.

Value

Named numeric vector of joint efforts (N m or N).

Examples

robot <- robot_example("planar1")
# Hold a horizontal 1 kg, 1 m rod against gravity along -y.
robot_inverse_dynamics(robot, 0, gravity = c(0, -9.81, 0))
#> joint1 
#>  4.905
